messages:
sam: quick note from today's sync: Dedicated pools causing unexpected p50 spikes when the router picks a cheaper model and the pool isn't warmed. want to nail down a clear admit contract between router and autoscaler so behavior is deterministic.
jane: agreed. the current "latency_preference" flag is too fuzzy. we need a small machine-readable SLO and a handshake.
kai: proposal: router sends candidate list + requested pctile/latency. autoscaler responds with a fast verdict: GRANT (reservation token), DEFER (ETA), or DENY. router retries next candidate on DENY or follows DEFER logic.
maria: ok but tokens introduce race conditions. what prevents a router from holding many tokens and not using them? we saw token hoarding before in other systems.
sam: token semantics: each GRANT returns token with ttl + max-concurrency field and a usage window. token must be redeemed within usage_window or autoscaler reclaims it. tokens are small opaque strings.
jane: also need a soft vs hard reservation distinction. GRANT can be provisional (warm path) or firm (dedicated slot). add a reservation_type flag.
kai: +1. also include a "bypass_level" in the response so billing/crediting logic knows if this used burst credits. router should attach tenant id and purpose to token to avoid cross-tenant replay.
maria: DEFER should include an ETA and a confidence score. router policy: wait if ETA < caller_max_wait and confidence > threshold, otherwise try next candidate. default caller_max_wait = 200ms.
sam: implementation concern: this /admit endpoint must be low latency (<20ms median) and extremely cheap to query. it can't be a heavy database operation. keep it in-memory cache + approximate admission.
kai: perf sketch: admit service keeps sliding-window occupancy estimates per pool and model, uses async warmup task to transition DEFER->GRANT. use statistical headroom (p95 request size).
jane: monitoring: admit_latency_ms, grant_rate, defer_rate, deny_rate, token_redeem_rate, token_expiry_rate, token_replay_attempts. alert if deny_rate > 0.5% for premium tenants.
maria: security: tokens should be signed (HMAC) and short lived. router verifies signature and TTL locally to avoid roundtrip in fast path. autoscaler keeps authoritative state to reclaim.
sam: test plan: 1) simulate 10k req/s with 10% bursty tenants. 2) fuzz router retry/backoff with DEFERs. 3) inject admission slowness to ensure router fallback logic works. 4) measure p50/p95 end-to-end.
kai: rollout: stage 0: dry-run headers logged only (no token enforcement). stage 1: enable admit on internal tenants (GRANT but not enforced). stage 2: token redemption enforced for internal canary. stage 3: opt-in customers. stage 4: global. each stage runs minimum 2 weeks for metrics.
jane: need migration plan for older router proto. we'll add new header X-Model-Admit and backward-compatible enum. small protobuf bump.
maria: action items: sam write API spec + token shape. kai implement /admit prototype w/ perf budget. jane own rollout checklist + canary gating. i'll add dashboards/alerts.
deploy-bot: autoscaler/admit-v1 queued for canary: deploy window 02:00-04:00 UTC, health-checks enabled, rollback on admit_latency > 50ms for 15m.
sam: thanks. i'll post the RFC follow-up with example headers and flow diagrams by EOD tomorrow. if nobody objects, i'll fold this into the autoscaler design doc. :thumbsup:
